headline: Nasdaq-100/S&P futures grind up off overnight lows toward session highs into the deep European morning (S&P futures ~7,825 vs. session range 7,773.75-7,838.50), VIX flat near 14.6, oil little changed (Brent ~$87) -- today's 12:30 UTC Retail Sales and 14:00 UTC preliminary UMich sentiment are the session's main checkpoints; Alpha Vantage remains fully rate-limited for a fifth consecutive run, so this assessment again relies entirely on WebSearch.
body: About two minutes past the top of the hour and roughly one hour past the prior run, and about 9.5 hours after Thursday's 20:00 UTC cash close, conditions remain calm into the deep European morning. S&P 500 futures have drifted up from the overnight session low (~7,773.75) toward the session high (~7,838.50), last quoted near 7,825.25 (session open 7,775.75), while Nasdaq 100 futures are only marginally firmer -- a modest, low-amplitude one-sided grind off the lows but with no confirmed failed-pullback or repeated-extension structure, continuing off Thursday's records (S&P 500 7,798.99, Nasdaq Composite 26,803.03) as the index complex heads for a third straight weekly advance. Dow futures were roughly flat to slightly softer, continuing the week's relative underperformance versus the S&P/Nasdaq. Asia's session again showed regional dispersion consistent with the prior run's characterization -- Kospi strength (AI/semiconductor-linked, Samsung and SK Hynix each up double digits on the week) alongside a more mixed picture elsewhere in the region -- MSCI Asia Pacific +0.3% on the day, +2.6% on the week, per Bloomberg's wrap, though this source substantially overlaps the prior run's and no materially fresher Asia close print was found this run, a genuine limitation. VIX holds flat near a fresh recent low, last quoted ~14.6 (little changed from the prior run's 14.53-14.70), and Brent crude is little changed near $87 as markets weigh renewed US threats against Iran and the prospect of a prolonged naval blockade against softer global-demand concerns -- a two-sided setup that argues for Stress rather than Tail. No fresh, index-relevant semiconductor or megacap catalyst was identified (Nvidia, AMD and broader chip-sector coverage found this run describes ongoing 2026 growth trends rather than a new overnight development); Applied Materials' contained post-earnings reaction remains company-specific across multiple runs with no evidence of broader transmission. Geopolitically, the Strait of Hormuz standoff remains unresolved under Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority permit regime, and the Ukraine-Russia war shows no fresh market-moving escalation; neither represents a new discontinuity since the prior run. Alpha Vantage's free-tier daily quota remains exhausted for a fifth consecutive run -- the TREASURY_YIELD call was retried once and returned an immediate rate_limit error both times -- so, per the fallback protocol, this assessment again relies entirely on WebSearch for yields, oil, VIX, equities and price-path context; a fresh, precisely-timestamped 10-year Treasury yield print could not be confirmed this run (last reliably observed ~4.65%, unchanged), which together with the continued Alpha Vantage outage and some residual cross-source dating overlap on the Asia figures keeps Confidence in the medium-low band, near the lower end of the recent range. Tail ticks up marginally to 10% (still low; the futures move is a modest grind off session lows, not observed persistent one-way efficiency with failed pullbacks) while Stress ticks up to 29% (from 27% last run) reflecting the approaching Retail Sales (12:30 UTC) and preliminary UMich sentiment (14:00 UTC) cluster, still the main driver of the forecast Stress path higher into midday UTC before easing back through the afternoon and into the next Asia handover.

lookbackSummary: Tail held in the low band (9-18%) through the full prior 24 hours as the index ground to a fresh S&P 500 record above 7,800 on soft PPI; Stress ran elevated to high (up to 58%) around the Wednesday/Thursday CPI-PPI and AMAT-earnings window before easing back into the low band (22-30%) by Friday's deep European morning as the after-hours reaction stayed contained to the single name and no broader transmission was confirmed.
outlookSummary: Tail is projected to stay low (9-14%) through the next 24 hours; Stress is projected to build from the high-20s toward the high-40s across the 12:30-14:00 UTC Retail Sales / UMich sentiment cluster before easing back through the afternoon and evening and into the next Asia handover, with no forecast slot currently implying an action change from EA_ON.

US pre-market positioning window; Retail Sales imminent at the top of the next hour. Tail stays capped absent observed persistent one-way price action in the Nasdaq-100 complex itself -- a single scheduled release is a checkpoint, not an automatic Tail escalation.

Retail Sales prints at 12:30 UTC (start of this slot); Stress is projected to build further into the print and the subsequent UMich release at 14:00 UTC, with dominant mode shifting to event/whipsaw reflecting the two-release cluster; any Tail escalation requires observed failed-pullback/persistent trend after the data, not the release itself.
